bug_semantics: ClaudeHookBridge handlePreToolUse makes its hard-deny decision on a target that extractTarget truncates with v.slice(0, 500) (and JSON.stringify(toolInput).slice(0, 300) as fallback), then returns allow/deny/ask without rewriting tool_input. Claude Code later executes the full untruncated Bash command field. An attacker (or compromised/constrained agent) can pad a command past 500 characters so denyPatterns never sees the dangerous suffix; in default observe mode that deny list is the only hard block, so the suffix runs. Same validator/executor mismatch class as a truncation-before-decision bypass (CWE-436).
flaw_origin: The truncation-before-decision mechanism was first written when ClaudeHookBridge was added in the v5.14.0 ecosystem-expansion commit. extractTarget was implemented to return a 500-character preview of command/file_path/url/etc., and handlePreToolUse immediately fed that preview into matchesAny(this.denyPatterns, toolName, target). No prior public tree contained ClaudeHookBridge, extractTarget, or denyPatterns matching.
